alt: Boeing's CST-100 Starliner spacecraft undocking from the International Space Station following its Crew Flight Test mission in 2024, floating in orbit with the Earth's limb visible below
story: A NASA Inspector General report published July 1, 2026 formally expressed doubt that Boeing's CST-100 Starliner will ever achieve human-rating certification — after $4.8 billion spent, repeated helium leaks, propulsion failures, and unresolved parachute anomalies — explicitly citing 'overconfidence in Boeing's heritage systems' and 'unrealistic launch schedules' as root causes, with the ISS due to retire around 2030.
why_funny: Boeing convinced NASA and Congress to fund a multi-decade space taxi entirely on the premise that their old aerospace skills were still reliable — the Inspector General's report is the official confirmation that they were not.
